q: A linear bounded automaton is a Turing machine that…
options: may only use the tape cells holding its input, between end markers
explain: The input sits between ⊢ and ⊣. The head may read and write anywhere inside, but never beyond the markers.
CSG ⇄ LBA is the type-1 level of the Chomsky hierarchy. PDAs give the context-free languages, and unrestricted TMs the recursively enumerable ones.

q: Membership (does the LBA accept w?) is decidable.
explain: True. On input w there are only finitely many configurations (states × head positions × tape contents). A run longer than that is looping, and a simulator can detect it and stop.

q: Emptiness (does an LBA accept any string at all?) is decidable.
explain: False. Emptiness for LBAs is undecidable, even though membership is decidable.

options: deterministic LBAs are as powerful as nondeterministic ones
LBAs can accept all context-free languages
explain: It is unknown whether DLBA = NLBA. It is known that CSLs are closed under complement (the Immerman–Szelepcsényi theorem).

q: An LBA has q states, tape alphabet Γ, and input length n. Roughly how many configurations can it be in?
explain: A configuration is a state, a head position among the n cells, and the contents of those n cells. That number is finite for each fixed n.

q: How does an LBA for {aⁿbⁿcⁿ} work?
options: Repeatedly cross off one a, one b and one c, and accept if they run out together
Push the a's on a stack and pop them on the c's
Copy the input to a second tape
explain: Marking symbols in place uses no extra tape, so the machine stays within the input region. One stack could only match two of the counts.

q: Order these by the languages they accept, from smallest class to largest: DFA, LBA, PDA, TM.
What do the end markers ⊢ and ⊣ do in an LBA?
options: Stop the head from leaving the input region
Mark the start and final states
Separate the input from the output
Mark the top of the stack
explain: The head may not move past ⊢ or ⊣, and the markers cannot be overwritten. That is what keeps the memory linear in the input size.

q: Which language can an LBA accept but a PDA cannot?
explain: {ww} is not context-free, but an LBA can find the middle and compare the two halves by marking cells in place. The others are context-free.
